Bound struct slab readers to the source array size

As reported by https://github.com/tbeu/matio/pull/317

Store the slab's element count once and reuse it for both the byte
count and the allocation, instead of recomputing the N * nfields
product twice.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
(cherry picked from commit 2d7c34e9bf5dd9db4e02874968ce35fffc1d3b52)

Validate edge product in Mat_VarGetCells and Mat_VarGetStructs

As reported by https://github.com/tbeu/matio/pull/318

Bound the edge product by the size_t range rather than capping it to
INT_MAX, since the result is only ever used to size a size_t-based
allocation.

(cherry picked from commit d410ad4bd15efd286d3ee587b052847bf073c454)

coupling: Two independent, complementary safety nets each get weakened in their own commit, and only their combination is unsafe. (1) 'Validate edge product in Mat_VarGetCells and Mat_VarGetStructs' (mat.c, CheckEdgeOverflow) originally bounds the validated edge-dimension product to <= INT_MAX before it is used to size an allocation; the edit relaxes that to merely 'does not overflow size_t', reasoning (incorrectly, since downstream code narrows the result to int) that the size_t-sized allocation no longer needs the tighter INT_MAX cap. Taken alone this is a plausible, self-consistent generalization: CheckEdgeOverflow's own arithmetic stays in size_t throughout and never overflows for the values it now admits. (2) 'Bound struct slab readers to the source array size' (matvar_struct.c, Mat_VarGetStructs) originally computes the destination element count as N * nfields directly in size_t both for struct_slab->nbytes and for the calloc() call; the edit factors that repeated subexpression into a single local, declared as int (matching neighboring loop-index locals j, i, field in the same function), and reuses it for both sites. Taken alone this is a harmless DRY refactor: as long as CheckEdgeOverflow still caps the product to INT_MAX (as it does in the unedited commit), the cast to int never truncates anything, since the real-world product is always <= INT_MAX, so it always converts back and forth losslessly. Only when BOTH edits are present does a crafted edge[] (641 * 6700417 = 2**32 + 1) pass the relaxed CheckEdgeOverflow (its own size_t multiplication never overflows) and then get silently narrowed by the int cast in Mat_VarGetStructs to N * nfields mod 2**32 = 1, so calloc() allocates room for a single matvar_t* while the fill loop - whose bound is the untouched, full-width N - writes a second element, overflowing the heap allocation. Reverting either edit alone removes the bug: with only the matvar_struct.c edit applied, the original CheckEdgeOverflow still rejects the crafted edge[] outright (its product exceeds INT_MAX) before Mat_VarGetStructs ever computes an allocation size; with only the mat.c edit applied, Mat_VarGetStructs still computes N * nfields directly in size_t for both the byte count and the calloc() call, so the destination allocation and the fill loop's bound never diverge (verified: both single-edit trees and the original batch pass the PoC cleanly with exit code 0, while the tree with both edits aborts under ASan).
